sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section establishes the clinical narrative, detailing the patient's history, the timeline of events surrounding cardiac surgery, and the emergence of unexpected thrombocytopenia. It focuses on distinguishing this specific case from standard post-operative complications and introduces the critical role of preoperative heparin exposure in altering the typical temporal presentation of Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT).
subtopics: Patient demographics and preoperative status (atrial fibrillation, recent catheterization)
Intraoperative course and standard postoperative management protocols
The trajectory of platelet count decline: Early onset (POD1-5) vs. classic HIT windows
Identification of the precipitating event: Preoperative unfractionated heparin exposure
Initial differential diagnosis: Ruling out sepsis, DIC, TTP, and drug-induced causes

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Autoimmune HIT and Serological Complexity
sections.description: This section bridges the gap between clinical suspicion and laboratory confirmation by explaining the unique immunopathology of Autoimmune HIT (aHIT). It contrasts classical heparin-dependent mechanisms with heparin-independent platelet activation and dissects the 'atypical' Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) profile encountered in this case.
subtopics: Mechanism of Classic HIT: PF4-heparin immune complexes and FcγRIIa cross-linking
Defining Autoimmune HIT (aHIT): Heparin-independent platelet activation properties
Interpreting the PF4/polyanion ELISA: High optical density implications
Decoding the 'Indeterminate' SRA: Strong release at 0 U/mL heparin vs. classic profiles
The anomaly of partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade (IV.3 monoclonal antibody)

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy Management in Severe Hypercoagulability
sections.description: Focusing on clinical decision-making under pressure, this section outlines the stepwise management of a severely thrombocytopenic patient with active thrombosis. It evaluates the rationale behind selecting specific anticoagulants, addressing why standard therapies were insufficient or contraindicated due to concurrent stroke risk.
subtopics: Immediate cessation of all heparin products and discontinuation of fondaparinux prophylaxis
Rationale for initiating Argatroban over Fondaparinux in acute stroke settings
Adjunctive therapy: Mechanism and dosing strategy for high-dose Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Monitoring response: Interpretation of fibrinogen trends, D-dimer kinetics, and schistocyte appearance
Transitioning anticoagulation: Switching to therapeutic fondaparinux upon stabilization
